title: The homogeneous sheaf action induces the graded cohomology module action
statement: Let A and B be commutative rings with an A-algebra structure on B. Let graded : N -> Submodule A B be an internal direct-sum decomposition of B, with 1 in graded(0), graded(k) graded(l) contained in graded(k+l), and algebraMap(A) contained in graded(0). Let f : X -> Spec A be a morphism of schemes and G_m be sheaves of O_X-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For b in graded(k), suppose there are O_X-linear maps mu_m(b) : G_m -> G_(m+k), additive in b, satisfying mu_(m+l)(b) composed with mu_m(c) = mu_m(bc), after the canonical degree transports. Suppose mu_m(algebraMap(a)) acts on every section by the restriction of f^sharp(a). Fix p >= 0 and write H_m = H^p(X,G_m) [pqf-def-cohomology]. Then there exists a B-module structure on the additive direct sum of H_m whose action sends b times the degree-m inclusion of x to the degree-(m+k) inclusion of H^p(mu_m(b))(x), for all homogeneous b and x. No properness, Noetherianity, quasi-coherence or finite-type condition is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 0897(1), the homogeneous action in the statement; its purely algebraic construction using additivity and functoriality of cohomology

proof.text: Apply additive cohomology to the homogeneous maps. Its preservation of addition and composition gives additive operators and the homogeneous product identity. The sectionwise scalar condition at a=1 identifies the degree-zero unit map with identity, so its cohomology map is identity.

Decompose each scalar uniquely into finitely many homogeneous terms using the internal grading; every vector in the additive direct sum also has finite support. Define the convolution action by these finite sums. Additivity follows termwise. Expand the finite double sums to check the product law using the homogeneous product identity; the unit identity gives one_smul. This is the required Module structure. The formula on homogeneous inclusions determines its whole action uniquely by distributivity.
